key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin with Gaussian-process surrogates supports rapid screening and simulated control of robotic welding conditions for future in-space metal joining.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help engineers narrow welding parameters and control strategies before costly thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware tests.
method: Model weld-pool heat transfer using finite volumes, phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure.
Compare Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates; assess gravity separately through a hydrostatic-to-capillary pressure ratio.
Simulate a six-axis robot welding an L-shaped seam, adjusting the power-source setting as travel speed changes.
evidence_signal: GPs achieved lower normalised MAE on all eight outputs; nominal 90% intervals covered 74/80 held-out solver responses, and finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; gravity is excluded from the thermal energy equation, and experimental validation remains necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
